description: Verifies the seal of a dataset. Short form: request is the run_dataset request as it was sent, and dataset_seal is the seal its answer gave. The plan is run again under run_dataset's permits and limits; the answer is holds, cause ("dataset_seal" when the seal given is not the seal the plan runs to), recomputed_dataset_seal when it holds (else no seal: run_dataset gives the true one), compared, and text_not_compared: no rows the agent holds are compared. A plan of solves is verified by this short form only. Long form: head, rows and frames_hex, the three parts a full answer carries (answer "full"), together, as they came. The rows, the root and the seal are recomputed, and row and fault name the first row changed, swapped, dropped or repeated; then the plan is run again under run_dataset's permits and limits and the engine's answer compared with it, value by value and byte for byte (cause answer_text, with differs_at and row): holds is true only when every byte is the engine's, values_hold when every value is. On this open connection a dataset is returned inline and holds at most 300 runs (OPEN_MAX_DATASET_ROWS), 1000000 steps in all (OPEN_MAX_DATASET_STEPS), 10000 frames and an answer counted from the plan at 4194304 bytes (OPEN_MAX_DATASET_ANSWER_BYTES) and 40000 characters, up to about 140 summary rows; a plan of solves holds the engine's own 64 and at most 15 s of them, or one, at each solver's measured time, which describe_solver states with the count (OPEN_PLAN_SECONDS). One address holds at most 1 physics permit at a time, and long work (a solve, a plan of runs or of solves, a run of more than 10000 steps, or a verification that computes one again) runs 1 at a time. A call that finds no permit or no place is answered "Too many concurrent physics tasks." and nothing waits: the same call sent later is answered once one is free. An answer is waited for 60 seconds, and long work is stopped there.

inputSchema.description: One of three forms. request and dataset_seal, the short form: the plan is run again and its seal compared. The three parts a full run_dataset answer carries (head, rows and frames_hex, all three required together, as they came), the long form: the rows, the root and the seal are recomputed from their exact values, then the head's plan is run again under the permits and the limits of run_dataset and the engine's full answer to it compared with the parts sent, value by value and then byte for byte, so a dataset that holds is every byte the engine's. dataset_seal alone: the stored dataset of that seal, its seals recomputed from its files and its plan run again into a folder of its own, the stored files compared with that run's byte for byte. The long form's answer carries holds, true when the answer sent is every byte the engine's, and values_hold beside it, true when every value of it is the engine's answer to its request computed again, whatever its spelling: each number by its 64-bit value, strings, flags and null exactly, keys and their order, the receipt string among them. A copy whose numbers a client wrote again in its own spelling (0.0001 for 1.0e-4, 12 for 12.0) has holds false and values_hold true, and differs_at names the first place its text differs.

dataset_seal.description: With request: the dataset_seal of the run_dataset answer, compared with the seal the plan runs to. Alone: the seal of a dataset stored as files (return "file"), read from the connection's own folder of that name. A dataset returned in the answer is not stored: it is verified with its request, or by its head, rows and frames_hex.

frames_hex.description: With head and rows: the frames a run_dataset answer carries, or null.

head.description: With rows and frames_hex: the head a run_dataset answer carries.

request.description: With dataset_seal alone: the run_dataset request as it was sent (the head's request). The plan is run again, under the permits and the limits of run_dataset, and its seal is compared with dataset_seal. Nothing is stored or read from storage, so it works whatever the return mode and on every connection. Its fields are run_dataset's. Worked example of the short form, as the whole arguments: {"request":{"domain":"energy","card":"thermal","plan":{"kind":"list","runs":[{"initial":{"temperature_k":293.15},"dt_s":1.0,"segments":[{"steps":60,"load":{"heat_power_w":5.0,"ambient_k":293.15}}],"record_every":60}]},"store":"none","return":"inline"},"dataset_seal":"<the dataset_seal of its run_dataset answer, 64 lowercase hex digits>"}.

rows.description: With head and frames_hex: the rows a full run_dataset answer (answer "full") carries.

name: verify_dataset
title: Verify dataset
